title: MV (DEMO 0.02) Ministry & Magic: Liturgy of the Living-Dead Librarians

posts.author: doomthey
posts.body:
MINISTRY & MAGIC: LITURGY OF THE LIVING-DEAD LIBRARIANS
​
SECTION A: SYNOPSIS
Spoiler
The ancestors speak, but do they listen?
For millennia, wizards known as
Librarians
have volunteered to rebuild the world that ancient cruel magic once enslaved and tore asunder. But when the discovery of powerful
Fusion Spells
spawns a new Golden Age of innovation, fears about a new Dark Age fester in its shadow as the revolution that freed the country thousands of years ago becomes a distant memory.
In search of knowledge of the lost past, you join an archaeology expedition and explore the depths hoping to discover what the past demands from the present. Little do you all know that the present has its own demands. Demands that may yet be heard.
After a
Living-Dead
, a spirit with a personality, rescues you from a cave-in and reluctantly claims to be a father of the revolution, you realize his comrades lie in rest across the country. Though they've hidden themselves away, their words and experiences may be just what the world needs.
With the guidance of these
Living-Dead Librarians
and your own experiences exploring the four corners of the country can you write a future that respects the past but refuses to imitate its mistakes?
MINISTRY & MAGIC: LITURGY OF THE LIVING-DEAD LIBRARIANS
is a 3D Strategy RPG made in RPG Maker MV where the only units are you and your arsenal of spells. With strong wits, these are more than enough to hold your own against the multitude of strange foes you'll encounter on your journey to connect past, present, and future.
-------
Imagine A World Unseen
: The spirituality and government structures of this world are inspired by those of ancient Nigerian and West African kingdoms and regions. Many of which are unlike any seen in the rest of the world. The way we organize the world is often taken for granted but when we visit new people, places, and time periods we may realize the human imagination is really broad! In this project, I wanted to explore my culture and sister cultures and share what I found in doing so (while also syncretizing it with the tradition of fantasy JRPGs and my own stylistic proclivities).
A 3D Battle System in RPG Maker?:
Using
MV3D
, the world is in full simplified 3D inspired by the recent influx of HD-2D RPGs and the PS1 era sprite-based 3D RPGs (thus I call this, Standard Definition-3D
). I've been working on how to utilize MV3D and
SRPG Engine
together and have finagled an approach that allows for 3D tactical battles. I'm still working on developing it further, but it's an exciting start and I'm hoping to share how I went about it sooner than later so other people can make similar games.
Combine Simple Spells into Powerful Incantations:
There 5 elements, Fire, Thunder, Water, Light, and Dark. Each element has its own unique attributes which can be altered with various modifier sigils, making for over 50 planned double-spell fusions. You will also learn complex
SUMMAs
, game-changing spells that combine 3 or more different sigils, invented by industrious librarians and laypeople alike. You can also develop them yourself through practice!
Meet Unique Living Cultures:
Anthropology is a big focus of this project. The country is made up of four Lands, dominant cultural and geographic regions, each with their own legends, traditions, architecture, clothing, and general ethos. Even within the Lands, from town to town you'll find that groups have their own way of expressing the same shared traditions! Learn about their cultures and help them out would you? That's the essence of the librarian liturgy: To help wherever you're best needed to the best of your ability.
Research Ancient Artifacts:
The Dark Age of Magic housed a deeply hierarchical and technological society unrecognizable from the current state of the country. Deep underground, perplexing structures and magical objects litter and pollute the world above them. These artifacts have gone unvisted and unresearched for thousands of years in fear of the curses they might hold. Yet, understanding them might allow you to draw parallels to the current age and empower yourself for future visits to the depths.

DISCLAIMERS
Spoiler
This game will have themes of (fictional) religion to explore certain concepts around cultural identity and flesh out what characters think of the magic system and society. There are themes of historical traumas and war due to the nature of the Dark Age having influences from feudalism (this shouldn't get much worse than the Shadow Temple from Ocarina of Time for a comparison).
These topics shouldn't get too heavy, the project is going for a mostly light tone, but these things are in there and are an important aspect of the message of the project.
[DOWNLOAD DEMO ON ITCH.IO]
Thanks so much for reading through! I've learned so much in my few years of working with RPG Maker and I thank the RPG Maker Forums for being so helpful to learn from. I'm hoping to carry this knowledge to other projects some day as well. I hope you enjoy what you've seen, I'd love your feedback and ideas. Wish me luck getting this project to completion!

Thank uu! Summoning guardians is definitely one of the spells I have planned. More broadly, you use elemental spells in combination with modifying spells like "Arrow" or "Blast" to change who they target and how powerful they are.
For example, an Arrow spell hits far away and targets every enemy in a straight line from you while a Blast spell hits every enemy adjacent to you for big damage. The idea is you have lots of spells catered to particular situations that help you deal with being outnumbered (e.g. you're fighting an enemy you don't want to get close to or you're fighting in an open area and are getting overwhelmed by foes).

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
I thought I'd offer an opinion after reading the name and description of the game.
The name (for a couple of reasons) implies a comedic tone which I don't think is what you're going for.
Reading the description, it seems like a serious setting and plot; and when you talk about paying homage to Nigerian spirituality and having a focus on anthropology, that sounds like you're taking the game seriously.
But, to me:
- Ministry & Magic sounds immediately like a spoof of the Ministry of Magic from Harry Potter. And I think a lot of gamers will make that association.
- Living-Dead sounds like an unrealistically clunky term. Whether it's one of the many existing words (ghost, vampire, zombie, wight, spirit, etc.) or something that's made up by the people in your setting, it doesn't sound believable to me that the people would use a hyphenate like that rather than a specific word.
It also sounds, again, like an intentional spoof of the Living Dead series of movies.
Finally, the alliteration of the subtitle (
Li
turgy of the
Li
ving-Dead
L
ibrarians) also lends a comedic or lighthearted air to it.
Take that as you like - obviously, it's just one person's opinion. Good luck with your project!

I appreciate the feedback!
I agree Living-Dead is probably a little bit of a mouthful
, I got it reading
African Religions & Philosophy
by John S. Mbiti for a class project. In some West African spiritualities
,
a person who dies has two stages of death: While a person has living relatives, they become a "Living-Dead", a spirit who still has a sense of personhood/individuation. It's once their last relative/friend in living memory passes away that they become a largely depersonalized spirit, indistinguishable from something like a force of nature.
In-game I'm imagining it's more of a technical term than common parlance, but I think it'll prove a helpful term to distinguish some of the types of spirits I have in the story I have planned!

posts.author: hiddenone
posts.body:
Heyas, I gave your demo a try. It's quite short but I think it gives a pretty good overview of what you're going for so good job.
I did have some issues with gameplay though.
Spoiler:
Feedback
I want to call out a huge positive first, thank you for having a field guide with tutorial reminders in the menu! It's really helpful for players who forget things or are coming back to play after a break, especially since this game requires the player to spin the camera to find paths using not-as-common buttons.
Personally I have issues with most 3D games in RPG Maker because they tend to be clunky to play. However, I think you've managed to take care of those issues pretty well here by locking the camera to set directions and keeping the maps relatively small. I did have trouble navigating due to the darkness and spinning the camera in some spots where the walls block my vision, but for the most part I could reorient myself and find the right way to go. It may be nice to up the brightness a bit in the maps though. I get that it's underground, but it is hard to see smaller details like the cracks in walls so playing around with the tint so that the screen is brighter but it still feels gloomy (up the grayscale or increase blue/green for example) would be a good idea.
Battles are probably where you want the most feedback, so I'm here with a bunch of little nitpicks. I was worried at first that the tactics-style battle system wouldn't play nice with the 3D, but I think you handled it pretty well. However, the lack of markers on the ground when moving and attacking really makes combat harder than it needs to be. The locked camera angle makes it difficult to judge where one tile ends and another begins, so figuring out if I'm close enough to an enemy is trial and error. I know some of the tactics battle systems have the option to show colorful squares on the ground, so you should turn that on if possible. If you don't want big squares then find a way to draw markings onto the ground, anything to help show how far the player can move and where attacks can reach. Another possibility would be to change how the selection square is displayed, so that it appears on the ground instead of upright facing the camera. A related but smaller issue is that the number that shows for movement is hard to read against the dark cave tiles, so consider changing it to be larger and outlined.
Combat itself (once I got to the right spot to attack), worked well. I like that you were very giving with the skill items, though I do wonder why they are called pearls in the world and pages in the spellbook. Not finding any fire attacks did mean that I mostly just punched the yellow crabs in the face and saved my Thunder skill for blue crabs, but for the start of the game that's not a big deal. Since the crystals are destructible in battles I'm curious if that will come into play more later, and if you'll be including skills that can lay traps instead of focusing only on straight-on attacks. The low number of enemies in most of the battles kept things from dragging on too long, but in the bigger fights the weakness of enemy AI really stood out. Often one or two crabs would just stand there doing nothing when the better option would have been to run away or move closer to attack. Adjusting how often the enemies use Wait in battles like that would be a good idea.
The battle simulator was a nice touch to show what other stuff will appear in battles later, but I do wish there were more enemies shown in it so I knew what other creatures I could look forward to fighting.
And there were some other minor things to think about:
Interesting use of 'jump' to choose the player character, but it's a bit jerky. Maybe stick with just speedily moving (or instant movement) to switch between them
Level up needs an explanation for what stats are affected by each choice
Make sure to tell your player when an on-map choice will use up an item. Breaking rocks uses Thunder, but the rock event doesn't mention that at all
Playtime seems to be tied to FPS, so my 140 FPS means time is moving twice as fast as it really should. Maybe find a way to lock FPS to 60
Overall, you have a solid concept and there seems to be a lot of story that will show up later. Right now polishing controls and the battle system's visuals will go a long way to making this game even better.
Good luck with your project!

I really appreciate the feedback!
One of the hardest parts of this project has been communicating where the player can move and who they can attack without ready-access to the traditional method of colored grid squares so I'm glad to have some feedback on this! in SRPG Core, I believe they use a bitmap overlaid on the 2D map to show where you can move and attack, so that feature doesn't work with MV3D natively. I think you offered a great intermediate solution in having the cursor become flat especially while the player selects their move. This helps a lot with depth perception and placement.
I'm glad that the 3D controls felt good. I got my inspiration for the camera controls from the Persona 2 Duology, I think they're good models for the kind of 3D RPG that MV3D lends itself to.
I'm also glad that the battles themselves went okay beyond the UI. My goal is to have the battles be brief and especially quick once you figure out the best positioning and develop a good strategy.
Lots of great suggestions! I'll keep them in mind as I develop the game further.

posts.author: doomthey
posts.body:
I'm considering retooling my magic-fusion system somewhat and I'm curious what people think:
Currently the way I have it set up is that you have elemental spell fragments (Fire, Lightning, Water) which interact with weaknesses/resistances system and also confer unique status effects (Fire is deals bonus damage, Lightning stuns, Water pushes). Then you have spell archetype pages (Arrow, Blast, Fortify, etc.) that determine the general shape or effect of the attack (e.g. Long Range Piercing Damage, Short Range big damage attack on all adjacent enemies, Gain this element's resistances and weaknesses). You fuse one of each to get an elemental spell with a particular attack type (Fire Blast: A high damage fire-type attack with bonus damage to all adjacent enemies)
With this system, I have a ton of different spell fusions and the system is easy to understand/predictable but somehow I worry I'm left with a huge number of uninteresting spells. I might be overthinking it, but when I play RPGs one of the most fun things for me is discovering and experimenting with spells that have more diverse effects and gravitas to them.
I'm brainstorming ideas to have more bespoke spells that still give the player a sense of crafting unique spells from basic parts. Here are a few ideas I've had so far:
-
Third tier fusion spells
: Fusion spells that use three materials and have uniquely powerful effects greater than the sum of their parts. (E.g. Water + Light + Fortify = Mirage Vest: Maximizes evasion for two turns.)
Pro:
We get more unique spell effects
Con:
We add spells but it doesn't do much for my "many boring spell" concern. As well, I can't add a third tier effect to every single combination due to not all of them being compelling and development constraints so I'd have to choose the most compelling ideas (which I suppose isn't inherently a problem).
-
Fourth tier fusion spells
: Game changing Fusion Spells use four materials and perhaps require a quest to learn them. (E.g. Water + Fire + Lightning + Blast = Delta Force: Almighty Non-Elemental Blast Damage)
Pro:
Even more unique spell effects, ties into game lore
Con:
Same as previous. Also, it may be difficult to balance these powerful spells to feel like a fair exchange for the number of materials involved without the strategy of the game becoming centered upon them.
- Instead of Fire, Lightning, and Water being flavors to add to spell archetypes, the elemental spells have inherent archetypes and the fusion system becomes about fusing them in a way that
masks different aspects of them to get the particular effect you want
. (E.g. Fire (Blast) + Lightning (Arrow) = Fire Arrow. Fire overtakes the Lightning element because Lightning is weak to Fire, creating a Fire spell with a long attack range.)
Pro:
It might diversify combat since basic magic spells have particular situations you need them for rather than being able to shoot them off whenever. It combines gameplay and worldbuilding somewhat.
Con:
This is a fair bit less intuitive than a Fire + Arrow = Fire Arrow system and I'm not sure that convolution adds much more fun.
In summary, I'm wondering if people prefer games that have more spells to meet every single situation or fewer more flashy/powerful spells? As well as if there is a golden mean between the two and where that lies? I'm curious if other people have experimented with magic fusion systems and if they've ran into similar concerns. Thanks for reading!
